Fix [#4213](https://github.com/PHPOffice/PhpSpreadsheet/issues/4213). Early versions of Php 8.4 caused problems for some Excel functions, among them ROUNDDOWN and ROUNDUP. New code was added which seemed to work for 8.4 and all prior releases (back to 7.4). However, as the issue shows, there is a problem with the new logic that had not been a problem for prior releases (PhpSpreadsheet 1.29.1 with Php 8.3 or earlier).

As it happens, some time after 8.4 broke the existing functionality, new features were added to it which enabled much cleaner logic. The code will now take this cleaner path when available, and revert to the older logic when not. This appears to work for all relevant Php releases, at least till the next non-match between PhpSpreadsheet and Excel is reported.

And, having made the change to ROUNDDOWN, it occurred to me that ROUNDDOWN always returns the same result as TRUNC (they differ only in number of required arguments). So I changed TRUNC to call ROUNDDOWN, and that didn't break anything. So I will keep that change. This probably means I should change Calculation so that ROUNDDOWN is called automatically, and deprecate TRUNC. That can happen at a later time.

- **`src/PhpSpreadsheet/Calculation/MathTrig/Round.php`** — `down()` (ROUNDDOWN) was using a broken `sprintf("%.1F")`-then-`round(HALF_UP)` approach that turned `249.9975 - 0.5 = 249.4975` into `249.5` and rounded up to `250`. Replaced with the correct version-gated logic:
  - PHP ≥ 8.4: `round((float)(string)$number, $digits, RoundingMode::TowardsZero)` (with `AwayFromZero` for `up()`).
  - PHP < 8.4: the half-step trick `round($number ∓ 0.5 * 0.1**$digits, $digits, PHP_ROUND_HALF_UP/DOWN)`, which correctly gives `249` and `-249`.
- **`src/PhpSpreadsheet/Calculation/MathTrig/Trunc.php`** — `TRUNC` now delegates to `Round::down()`, since TRUNC and ROUNDDOWN are equivalent.
